comparison_evidence.scope: Function and contract comparison against the existing NOAA GML global CH4 annual growth adapter and the DOI-keyed Crossref/OpenAlex adapters. CO2 and CH4 are distinct species with different fixed source tables and units; neither gas-specific adapter supplies the other gas. This supports coexistence by task, not comparative reliability, latency, quality, or cost.
findings: The NOAA CO2 table returns carbon-dioxide annual increments and uncertainty in ppm; the existing CH4 table returns methane increments in ppb. Their input/output units and fixed paths are species-specific, so both tools remain useful for different research questions.
The CH4 tool cannot satisfy a CO2/ppm request; Crossref and OpenAlex are bibliographic metadata tools rather than atmospheric observation readers.
No performance or cost superiority is claimed; live service quality and comparable cost remain unknown.
